description: Flown by Neil Armstrong and David Scott on 16 March 1966 on the first orbital docking; the museum centrepiece and confirmed on the museum's own current exhibitions page in 2026

One of only two surviving F5D-1s; delivered to the US Navy then transferred to NASA Flight Research Center in 1961 as NASA 802 and flown by Neil Armstrong in Dyna-Soar abort-manoeuvre development; NASA's own airframe-disposition page places it at Wapakoneta; displayed outdoors; year_built left blank because only the 1956 production-run year is known and that is not a delivery date

Serial 28-001 and the first Learjet 28 and the first production jet with winglets; Neil Armstrong set five FAI records in it in February 1979; donated by Kevin Hayward of Ox Industries and flown to Neil Armstrong Airport at New Knoxville on 5 August 2020 for the museum; an on-site historical marker confirms it in place

Displayed inside the museum mounted in a climbing attitude; the museum's own caption describes it as the type Neil Armstrong learned to fly in rather than his actual aeroplane; registration not established from any source so the tail number is deliberately blank
